title: Microsoft Teams: Copilot in the Queues app on mobile
summary: The briefing's rollout, licensing, default state and controls are supported. Minor corrections should preserve Microsoft's expected completion wording, name the Graph license-assignment body properties and complete the recording-template creation route.

claims.claim: It can take up to 48 hours after Teams Premium licensing for the Queues app to appear.
claims.quote: Once a user is licensed for Teams Premium, it can take up to 48 hours for Queues app to be available in the Teams client.

claims.claim: The Queues app is enabled by default for Teams users assigned Teams Premium and Teams Phone who are voice enabled.
claims.quote: Queues app is enabled by default for all Teams users in your organization who are assigned both a Teams Premium and Teams Phone license and who are voice enabled.

claims.claim: The Queues app supports iOS and Android mobile clients.
claims.quote: The Queues app is currently supported on Teams desktop, Mac, and Virtualized Desktop Infrastructure (VDI) clients, Teams phones (touch devices only), and iOS and Android mobile clients.

claims.claim: With auditing enabled, Copilot user interactions are automatically logged.
claims.quote: The system automatically logs these activities as part of Audit (Standard). If your organization enables auditing, you don't need to take extra steps to configure auditing support for Copilot and AI applications.

claims.claim: The general Copilot audit rules cover this Copilot experience when auditing is enabled.

claims.quote: This hidden folder isn't designed to be directly accessible to users or administrators, but instead, store data that compliance administrators can search with eDiscovery tools.

claims.quote: surface relevant information and insights from the conversation, helping them get up to speed and take the next step without having to review the entire call

claims.quote: Searched: "Queues" "Copilot" "mobile"; site:learn.microsoft.com/microsoftteams "Copilot" "Queues app" mobile. Read manage-queues-app and release-notes; results describe mobile Queues support and desktop Copilot, not a dedicated mobile feature page.

claims.claim: Microsoft 365 admin center > Billing > Licenses > product > Assign licenses reaches licence assignment.
claims.quote: In the admin center, go to the Billing > Licenses page. Select a product. On the product details page, select Assign licenses.

claims.claim: POST /v1.0/users/{id | userPrincipalName}/assignLicense assigns or removes user licences.
claims.quote: POST /users/{id | userPrincipalName}/assignLicense. addLicenses: objects that specify the licenses to add. removeLicenses: A collection of skuIds that identify the licenses to remove. Required. Can be an empty collection.
claims.fix: Keep the call and add to controls[0].note: 'The request body uses addLicenses to add licences and removeLicenses to remove licence skuIds; removeLicenses is required and can be empty.'

claims.claim: Delegated licence assignment requires a supported Entra role such as License Administrator or User Administrator, or a custom role with microsoft.directory/users/assignLicense.
claims.quote: the signed-in user must be assigned a supported Microsoft Entra role or a custom role with the microsoft.directory/users/assignLicense role permission. The following least privileged roles are supported for this operation: Directory Writers; License Administrator; User Administrator

claims.claim: LicenseAssignment.ReadWrite.All is the least privileged application permission for licence assignment.
claims.quote: | Application | LicenseAssignment.ReadWrite.All | AgentIdUser.ReadWrite.All, AgentIdUser.ReadWrite.IdentityParentedBy, Directory.ReadWrite.All, User.ReadWrite.All |

claims.claim: Teams admin center > Voice > Call queue > call queue > Templates > Automatic recording template selects the recording template.
claims.quote: go to Voice > Call queue. Select the call queue you want to have automatic recording for. On the Templates tab, scroll to find the Automatic recording template section. Select the automatic recoding template template from the dropdown.

claims.claim: Set-CsCallQueue -Identity <Guid> -AutoRecordingTemplateId <String> applies an automatic recording template, subject to the stated private-preview restriction.
claims.quote: Set-CsCallQueue -Identity <Guid> ... [-AutoRecordingTemplateId <String>]. The AutoRecordingTemplateId parameter indicates the Auto Recording template to apply to the call queue.

claims.claim: The automatic recording template is created under Voice > Templates and resources.
claims.quote: go to Voice > Templates and resources. Select Templates. Select Automatic Recording as the template type. Select Add to create a new Automatic Recording template.
claims.fix: Replace 'Template created under Voice > Templates and resources' with 'Template created under Voice > Templates and resources > Templates > Automatic Recording > Add'.

claims.claim: The Set-CsCallQueue reference restricts AutoRecordingTemplateId to Voice applications private preview customers.
claims.quote:
### -AutoRecordingTemplateId
Voice applications private preview customers only.

claims.claim: The Set-CsCallQueue reference warns that saving the queue through Teams admin center removes this setting.
claims.quote: Saving a call queue configuration through Teams admin center will remove this setting.

claims.claim: The call queue setup page says automatic recording can be configured via PowerShell in its August 13, 2026 entry.
claims.quote:
August 13, 2026
Automatic Recording for Call Queue can be configured via PowerShell.

claims.claim: Teams admin center > Voice > Calling policies > policy > Copilot reaches the general calling-policy Copilot control.
claims.quote: Expand Voice from the navigation pane. Under Voice, select Calling policies. Either select an existing policy or create a new one. From the dropdown for the Copilot setting, select On, On with saved transcript required, or Off.

claims.claim: Set-CsTeamsCallingPolicy -Identity <policy name> -Copilot Disabled turns off Copilot for calls governed by that policy.
claims.quote: To turn off Copilot for calls, use the following command: Set-CsTeamsCallingPolicy -Identity <policy name> -Copilot Disabled

claims.claim: The calling-policy documentation covers one-to-one and group calls and identifies 1:1 Teams and PSTN calls as its scope.
claims.quote: APPLIES TO: 1:1 Teams calls Public Switched Telephone Network (PSTN) calls. Teams calling policies control Copilot in one-to-one and group calls.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not confirmed the calling-policy Copilot setting controls recorded queue-call Copilot in the Queues app.
claims.quote: Searched: site:learn.microsoft.com/microsoftteams "Copilot" "call queue" policy; site:learn.microsoft.com/powershell/module/microsoftteams "Queues" "Copilot". Read Copilot calling guidance, Queues app and release notes; none connects that policy to queue-call recap.

claims.claim: Teams admin center > Teams apps > Manage apps > Actions > Org-wide app settings > Microsoft apps reaches the documented Queues app disabling control.
claims.quote: Navigate to Teams apps > Manage apps. Select Actions > Org-wide app settings > Microsoft apps. Select Off and Save.

claims.claim: No automation equivalent is documented for this org-wide Microsoft apps setting used to disable Queues.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams Queues app org-wide Microsoft apps disable PowerShell Set-CsTeamsAppPermissionPolicy; "Org-wide app settings" "Microsoft apps" PowerShell; "Microsoft apps" "Set-CsTeamsClientConfiguration". Read Queues guidance and returned module excerpts; no equivalent.

claims.claim: The documented org-wide Off setting disables the whole Queues app rather than only its Copilot capability.
claims.quote: You can turn off the Queues app via the Teams admin center. However, doing so also turns off other Microsoft apps like Insights and Tasks.

claims.claim: Turning that setting Off also turns off Insights and Tasks.
claims.quote: However, doing so also turns off other Microsoft apps like Insights and Tasks.

claims.where: controls[4].ui; controls[4].api; Change & support; Governance guidance
claims.claim: A separate tenant switch for Copilot in the mobile Queues app is not documented on either the UI or automation surface.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot Queues app mobile shared call history permissions disable Copilot policy; site:learn.microsoft.com/powershell/module/microsoftteams "Queues" "Copilot". Read Queues app, Copilot calling guidance and release notes; no separate mobile Queues Copilot switch.

claims.claim: The recording template controls recorded-call availability, not a separate Copilot on/off setting.
claims.quote: An automatic recording template for Call Queue defines where, in SharePoint, recordings and transcripts will be stored, the prompts played to callers to let them know that recording is enabled, and defines who has access to the recordings.

claims.claim: Licence assignment is the documented user-level way to decide who gets this Copilot experience; no separate Queues Copilot eligibility policy is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: "Queues" "Copilot" "permissions"; site:learn.microsoft.com/microsoftteams "Copilot" "call queue" policy. Read MC1552391, Queues guidance, calling guidance and release notes; licences are required and no separate Queues Copilot eligibility policy is specified.

claims.claim: The October 27, 2026 Microsoft 365 Copilot release notes describe desktop Copilot in the Queues app.
claims.quote:
## October 27, 2026
Updates released between October 13, 2026, and October 27, 2026.
Use Copilot Chat after a call in Queues app [Windows, Mac]

claims.claim: The documented desktop flow opens a recorded call from unified call history, selects Recap and launches the Copilot Chat sidecar.
claims.quote: Open the Queues app and select a recorded call from unified call history. Select the Recap tab and launch the Copilot Chat sidecar. Ask Copilot to summarize the call or answer questions about specific details discussed.
